assessment: Reveal only after all seven fits per date and all three dates freeze. Compare algorithm changes at 220 fields, source union under original HGB, and both together. Check same-policy asset/date gains; these dates cannot be independent confirmation.
blends: Six new XGBoost models each averaged 50/50 with saved observation neural. Three combined-feature XGBoost models each averaged 50/50 with the new combined HGB. New combined HGB averaged 50/50 with saved observation neural. No outcome-selected blend weights.
controls: Existing seven-leaf HGB additionally fits the 399-column union. Thirteen saved sources include original, context, spot and 100ms Bybit top1/top25 tree/neural/blend controls. Different algorithms have different split rules and compute costs; do not claim exact capacity matching.
hessian_units: min_child_weight is a summed Hessian-mass bound and is not equivalent to the HGB minimum leaf count of 100.
hypothesis: The existing seven-leaf trees may miss nonlinear interactions between own context, spot flow and foreign liquidity. Combining observed sources and changing the boosting algorithm/capacity may improve the unchanged five-second forecast.
posterior_contract: Equal asset weight. Balanced losses also equalize each asset/class; recover p by normalizing raw q times that asset training prior. Natural losses use equal asset weighting only and normalize raw q directly. Class indices 0/1/2 map exactly to -1/0/+1.
preprocessing: Quantile limits 0.001/0.999 fitted to pooled training features only, matching HGB limits. XGBoost hist uses float32 matrices and a numeric asset indicator. Fixed 400 rounds; no early stopping, assessment fitting or validation selection.

representations.combined: Original 220 context plus 98 own/peer Bybit top25 fields at 100ms plus 81 own/peer spot-trade fields at 100ms, totaling 399
